messages:
eva: heads up — started seeing a sharp p95/p99 regression for tenant acme-inc on /v1/chat around 03:40 UTC. p99 jumped from ~0.9s to ~3.2s. dashboard shows a massive increase in kv-prefix cache miss rate and eviction churn. filing since support ticket #2321 flagged customer impact.

mike: can you paste the short traces and any kv metrics? curious if it's a warmup surge or thrash from key entropy.

eva: putting snippets below. logs show many 'kv_cache: miss' lines followed by immediate evictions. stack traces point to prefix normalization returning different normalized keys for same logical prefix after unicode trimming change.

```
# from runtime logs
[03:40:12] request_id=abc123 tenant=acme path=/v1/chat latency=3120ms stage=generate kv_cache=miss key="/acme/conv/\u00A0input" 
[03:40:12] cache_evict key="/acme/conv/input" reason=LRU_shrink
[03:40:12] request_id=abc123 stage=model_infer latency+=3100ms
```

# kv stats (prom):
kv_prefix_hit_rate: 0.12 -> 0.03
kv_eviction_rate: increase 6x over baseline
cpu on worker: 85% -> 98% due to cache rebuild
```

raj: oof. that normalization change landed in runtime v2.11 yesterday, right? could be producing both \u00A0 (NBSP) and normal space variants causing duplicate keys. eviction churn would explain p99 spikes as hot prefixes keep missing.

mike: quick repro steps? want to confirm locally.

eva: repro curl below (uses tenant acme, small seq length):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"prefix":"/acme/conv/\u00A0input"}'
```

Doing that a few times alternately with prefix containing normal space yields two different cache keys and evicts the hot entry repeatedly.

sre-oncall: if we confirm it's the normalization bug, mitigation options: rollback v2.11 normalization change (fast but risky), deploy hotfix to normalization function (small patch), or patch eviction policy to be less aggressive for recently-seen prefixes (increase TTL or make eviction conservative for hot keys). Also temporary routing: steer acme traffic to a dedicated instance pool with larger KV residency.

support-bot: escalation created: INC-2321. Severity set to P1 due to customer SLA impact. Notifying account team.

raj: for quick short-term relief I'd suggest two-pronged: 1) add a fallback normalization step that normalizes NBSP->space at input boundary and backfill cache warmup for top N prefixes. 2) increase prefix cache high-water mark for the next 2 hours for the affected region. Both are low-risk config changes.

mike: agree on short-term. I'm pushing a config to increase prefix cache capacity and relax LRU bias for 30m. will also add a canary patch to normalize NBSP->space at ingress for tenant acme only.

eva: thanks. I'll coordinate with support to notify customer and provide repro and ETA. will attach sample logs to ticket.

sre-oncall: action items:
- mike: temp config bump + canary normalization (owner) — target +15m
- raj: prepare normalization patch (unit tests + integration) — ETA 2h
- eva: customer comms and attach traces to INC-2321 — immediate
- mike: revert config bump after 2h and monitor metrics

mike: pushed canary ingress normalization for acme to staging and a small capacity bump to prod in region eu-west-1. monitoring p95/p99 now.

[10m later] eva: quick update — p99 down to ~1.0s, p95 back to baseline. kv_prefix_hit_rate improving. customer acknowledged reduction in tail latency. keeping incident open until normalization patch lands and backfill completes.

raj: I'll land the normalization fix with tests and a small migration to normalize historical keys during quiet window tonight. plan to emit a one-time metric kv_key_normalizations to validate backfill coverage.

mike: noted we should also add a regression test in our e2e harness that fuzzes unicode whitespace in prefixes to catch this class of bug. adding TODO.

support-bot: INC-2321 updated: mitigation in place, customer notified, escalation remains open until patch deploy.

eva: closing loop — great quick triage. leaving follow-ups in INC-2321 and will post a short postmortem if backfill causes any secondary effects. :thumbsup:
